title: Philippine passport: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Filipino citizens applying for a first passport, renewing, replacing a lost or damaged one, or applying for a child under 18. Only Filipino citizens can get a Philippine passport. [1]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: fees
content:
What it costs: ₱950 regular processing or ₱1,200 expedited, the same for new and renewal. [1] Payment centres add a ₱50 convenience fee. [8] Lost, damaged or mutilated passports add a ₱350 penalty. [3] Booking the appointment is free. [1]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: processing time
content:
How long it takes: Regular: 10 working days in Metro Manila (NCR), 12 working days outside NCR. Expedited: 5 working days in NCR, 7 outside NCR. Abroad: about 4 to 6 weeks. These dates are tentative and do not include courier delivery. [1]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: requirements (part 1 of 2)
content:
- Book a confirmed online appointment at passport.gov.ph. Appointments made anywhere else are not legitimate. Courtesy Lane applicants (seniors, PWDs, pregnant women, solo parents, OFWs, children 7 and below) may walk in. [1] [7]
- Print the application form and e-receipt generated after booking and payment. [1]
- New adult applicants: bring your PSA birth certificate on security paper (original and photocopy). [2]
- New adult applicants: bring one acceptable valid ID with one photocopy, e.g. PhilID/ePhilID, UMID, SSS card, LTO driver's licence, PRC ID, voter's ID or certificate, postal ID. Pag-IBIG, TIN and PhilHealth IDs are not accepted. [5] [1]
- Renewing: bring your current ePassport with a photocopy of the data page. [3]
- Married women using the spouse's surname: bring your PSA marriage certificate. You do not need it if you keep your maiden name. [2]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: requirements (part 2 of 2)
content:
- Minors (under 18): bring the child's PSA birth certificate, a valid ID for the child and for the accompanying adult, and a notarised Special Power of Attorney (SPA) if a parent will not appear. If the parents are not married, the mother accompanies the child or signs the SPA. [4]
- Lost passport: bring a police report in English and a notarised affidavit of loss. You pay a ₱350 penalty. [3]
- Late-registered birth certificate: bring an extra primary ID, or two of: NBI clearance, school records, government service record, or PhilHealth Member Data Record. [2]
You do not need to bring a passport photo. DFA captures your photo and biometrics on site. [1]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: steps
content:
1. Go to passport.gov.ph and choose Schedule an Appointment. [6]
2. Pick the DFA consular office or Temporary Off-site Passport Services (TOPS) site, date and time. [1]
3. Fill in the online form exactly as your PSA documents read. Major errors can lead to rejection. [1]
4. Pay the processing fee (₱950 regular or ₱1,200 expedited) through an accredited payment channel. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable. [1] [6]
5. Print the confirmation, application form and receipt from your email. If no email arrives within 24 hours of paying, call (02) 8234-3488. [1]
6. Arrive on your appointment date with your originals and photocopies.
7. Have your photo, fingerprints and signature captured at the consular office. [1]
8. Keep your official receipt. It shows the tentative release date. [1]
9. Claim the passport at the same office where you applied, or wait for courier delivery if you chose it. [1]
10. Check every detail on the data page before you leave. [1]
Source: https://passport.gov.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: after you apply
content:
- Validity: 10 years if you were 18 or older when you applied, 5 years if you were under 18. This comes from Section 12 of RA 11983 (New Philippine Passport Act, 2024), which repealed RA 8239 as amended (including RA 10928). The DFA FAQ refers to this rule as "Section 10". [7] [1]
- Someone else claiming: an immediate family member needs an authorisation letter. Anyone else needs a Special Power of Attorney (SPA). Both must bring the IDs, the DFA receipt and, for renewals, the old passport. [1]
- Unclaimed passports are cancelled one year after the release date. [1]
- Renewal: you may renew at any time. DFA suggests renewing within one year of expiry. There is no penalty for renewing an expired passport. Most countries need at least six months of validity for travel. [1]
- Old visas stay valid in your old passport. Carry both passports. [1]
- Do not buy plane tickets until you have the passport in hand. [6]
Source: https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_11983_2024.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Philippine passport: problems and where to get help
content:
- No slots showing: refresh the booking page later, because slots open from time to time. [1]
- Missed appointment: you can reschedule only for exceptional or emergency reasons, within 6 months of the original date, by emailing the consular office. [1]
- Error printed in the passport: reapply and pay ₱950. [1]
- Name or date mismatch in documents: fix the PSA record first (RA 9048/10172 annotation) before applying. [2]
- Fixers: using them is illegal and carries penalties under RA 11983. [7]
Help: Appointment hotline (02) 8234-3488. Consular inquiries (02) 8651-9400. Mobile 0956-052-6290 (Globe) or 0961-943-2021 (Smart). [1] Email [passportconcerns@dfa.gov.ph](mailto:passportconcerns@dfa.gov.ph) or [oca.concerns@dfa.gov.ph](mailto:oca.concerns@dfa.gov.ph). [6]
Source: https://consular.dfa.gov.ph/passport-faq/ (checked 2026-10-09).

title: NBI clearance: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Anyone who needs an NBI clearance for work, travel, a visa or another transaction. This covers first-time applicants and renewals. Foreign nationals can apply for the first time only at the NBI Main Office or regional offices. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: fees
content:
What it costs: ₱160 total. This is ₱130 for the clearance plus ₱30 e-payment convenience fee. First-time jobseekers with a barangay certificate pay nothing (RA 11261). [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: processing time
content:
How long it takes: Same visit if you have no "hit" (name match). If you have a hit, the release date is about 8 working days later at the Main Office, or 15 working days at regional, district and satellite clearance centres. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: requirements
content:
- Prepare an email address and mobile number for the online account at clearance.nbi.gov.ph. [1]
- Get your original PhilSys National ID, or two other valid IDs. Accepted IDs include passport, driver's licence, UMID, PRC ID, postal ID, voter's ID, PSA birth certificate, or school ID with registration form. [1]
- First-time jobseekers: get a barangay certificate stating you have lived there for at least 6 months, and sign the oath of undertaking. [1] [3]
- Renewing: keep your old clearance number. Online renewal is open only to people whose last clearance was issued on or after 16 Oct 2016 and had no hit. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: steps
content:
1. Register or log in at clearance.nbi.gov.ph and complete your personal details. [1]
2. Choose Apply for clearance, then pick an NBI clearance centre and an appointment date. [1]
3. Pay ₱160 (₱130 + ₱30) through the e-payment options shown, and keep the reference number. [1]
4. Go to the clearance centre on your schedule and bring your IDs and reference number. [1]
5. Have your photo, fingerprints and signature captured. [1]
6. Wait for your printed clearance, which takes about 15 minutes if there is no hit. [1]
7. If you have a hit, return on the release date given. You may be asked to appear for a Quality Control interview. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: online renewal (no visit needed for biometrics)
content:
1. Log in at clearance.nbi.gov.ph and choose renewal using your previous clearance details. [1]
2. Choose pick-up at the NBI Clearance Building, UN Avenue, Manila (ready after 24 hours), or courier delivery. Delivery costs ₱200 in NCR (about 5 working days) and ₱350 outside NCR (about 7–10 working days). [1]
3. Pay the clearance fee and any delivery charge online. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: after you apply
content:
- Priority lanes serve senior citizens, PWDs, pregnant women and frontliners. [1]
- Before submitting your clearance: Check the requirements of the office requesting it, including how recently it must have been issued.
- A hit does not mean you have a criminal record. It means your name matches or resembles a name in NBI records and must be checked by hand. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: NBI clearance: problems and where to get help
content:
- Paid, but the status is not updating: keep the payment reference number and email the NBI. [1]
- Older fee figures online (₱115, ₱155, ₱165): these come from older charters or other payment channels. The 2025 Charter lists ₱130 + ₱30. [1] [2]
Help: Email [ncic@nbi.gov.ph](mailto:ncic@nbi.gov.ph). Visit the NBI Clearance Building, UN Avenue, Ermita, Manila. For complaints, call the 8888 Citizens' Complaint Hotline or the Civil Service Contact Center ng Bayan (CCB) at 1-6565. [1]
Source: https://nbi.gov.ph/uploads/2025/04/2025-CITIZENS-CHARTER-HANDBOOK-1st-EDITION.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): who can apply
content:
Who this is for: First-time employees, self-employed people and professionals, mixed-income earners, and people who need a TIN only for a one-time transaction or a government ID (EO 98).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): fees
content:
What it costs: Free for employees, one-time and EO 98 applicants. Self-employed and mixed-income registrants pay ₱30 documentary stamp tax (DST) on the Certificate of Registration (COR). The old ₱500 Annual Registration Fee no longer applies. (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025; RR 7-2024; RMC 14-2024)
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/BIR%20Citizen's%20Charter%202025%202nd%20Edition%20v2.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): processing time
content:
How long it takes: Walk-in, 6 hours (Form 1902 or 1904). Online through your employer on ORUS, 2 days, 7 hours and 55 minutes. Online for business, 3 days. (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025)
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/BIR%20Citizen's%20Charter%202025%202nd%20Edition%20v2.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): which form is yours?
content:
- Your situation: Employee (purely compensation); BIR form: 1902; Deadline to register: Within 10 days from the start of employment (RR 7-2024)
- Your situation: Self-employed, professional, or mixed income (job plus business); BIR form: 1901; Deadline to register: On or before you start the business. That is your first sale, or 30 days after your Mayor's Permit, PTR or DTI/SEC registration, whichever comes first (RR 7-2024)
- Your situation: One-time transaction (for example, selling property or settling an estate), or a TIN only for a government ID under EO 98; BIR form: 1904; Deadline to register: Before payment of the tax (one-time), or whenever you need it (EO 98) (RR 7-2024)

The current form versions are the October 2025 editions (RMC 97-2025, 30 Oct 2025). Download them from the BIR website. Older versions may be refused.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): requirements
content:
- Check that you have never had a TIN. If you once had one, even from a past job, use it. Do not apply for a second TIN.
- Prepare one government ID that shows your name, address and date of birth, for example your PhilSys ID or passport (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- If you are a married woman using your married name, bring your marriage contract (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- If you are a first-time jobseeker, get a barangay certification. It is listed as an extra document (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- If you are applying online, take a selfie holding your ID (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- Self-employed: get your DTI certificate (or SEC/CDA papers) and Mayor's Permit or PTR first, if you already have them. Check the full list in the registration checklist (RMC 74-2025).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/BIR%20Citizen's%20Charter%202025%202nd%20Edition%20v2.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): steps: new employee
content:
1. Give your new employer your personal details and ID within your first days at work.
2. Ask your employer to apply for your TIN through the Employer Service Link on ORUS. New hires without a TIN are registered by their employer online (RR 7-2024; BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
3. Wait for the TIN, which arrives in about 2 days, 7 hours and 55 minutes. There is no fee (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
4. Keep the TIN for life. Employees do not get a Certificate of Registration (RR 7-2024).
If your employer cannot apply for you, you may walk in. Fill out Form 1902 and file it at the RDO that covers your employer. Walk-in processing takes 6 hours and is free (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
Source: https://orus.bir.gov.ph (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): steps: self-employed, professional or mixed income
content:
1. Create an account on ORUS.
2. Choose individual business registration and fill out the Form 1901 details.
3. Upload your ID, your selfie holding the ID, and your business documents.
4. Pay the ₱30 DST for your Certificate of Registration (RR 7-2024; BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
5. Wait for your eCOR. Processing takes about 3 days (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
6. Get your invoices authorized (Authority to Print, or a permit for loose-leaf or computerized invoices) (RR 7-2024).
7. Register your books of accounts (RR 7-2024).
8. Attend the RDO's briefing for new registrants (RR 7-2024).
9. Post your COR at your place of business. If you sell online, post it on your page or website (RR 7-2024).
Mixed-income earners who already have a TIN from employment do not get a new TIN. File Form 1905 to update their registration instead (RMC 97-2025).
Source: https://orus.bir.gov.ph (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): steps: one-time transaction or EO 98 (TIN for an ID)
content:
1. Fill out Form 1904 (RMC 97-2025).
2. Submit it on ORUS, or at the RDO for your residence. For a one-time transaction, submit it at the RDO that handles the transaction (RR 7-2024).
3. Receive your TIN. Walk-in takes 6 hours and ORUS takes 3 days. Both are free (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2097-2025.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): after you apply
content:
- Digital TIN ID: From 24 April 2026, the BIR Digital TIN ID is available in the eGovPH app. The ORUS Digital TIN ID counts as a valid government ID (RMC 34-2026, 28 Apr 2026).
- Self-employed: Ask your RDO to confirm the tax returns and filing deadlines that apply to your business after registration.
- Registration seal badge: Businesses must display the BIR Registration Seal badge. The deadline was extended to 31 October 2026 (RMC 99-2026, 24 Sep 2026).
- No yearly fee: The ₱500 Annual Registration Fee was removed from 22 January 2024. You no longer need Form 0605 for it (RMC 14-2024; RR 7-2024).
- Late registration: Contact your RDO for the applicable requirements and an assessment of any penalties.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20NO.%2034-2026.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number): problems and where to get help
content:
- "I already have a TIN from a past job." Do not apply again. Have it transferred to your new RDO by filing Form 1905 (RMC 97-2025).
- "ORUS rejected my ID." Check that the ID shows your name, address and birth date, and that your selfie is clear (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- BIR Contact Center: (02) 8538-3200 and [contact_us@bir.gov.ph](mailto:contact_us@bir.gov.ph) (BIR Contact Us).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2097-2025.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): who can apply
content:
Who this is for: SSS members with a permanent SS number and a My.SSS account who want the MySSS Card (the UMID replacement). [1]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CI2025-008-External.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): fees
content:
What it costs: SSS charges nothing to apply, but the partner bank may charge the cost of the card and its own fees. Check with your chosen bank. [1] [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CI2025-008-External.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): processing time
content:
How long it takes: The card arrives within 15 working days in Metro Manila, or 20 working days elsewhere, after the bank opens your account. [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/mysss-card/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): requirements
content:
- Make sure your SS number is permanent, not temporary. [1]
- Register for a My.SSS account at member.sss.gov.ph if you do not have one. [2]
- Check that your local address, mobile number and email are updated in SSS records. [1]
- Register for the PhilSys National ID. SSS verifies you through National ID eVerify. [1] [2]
- Use a phone with a working camera for the facial scan. [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CI2025-008-External.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): steps
content:
1. Log in to My.SSS and go to Services → MySSS Card. [2]
2. Confirm that your personal details are correct. [2]
3. Give consent for National ID eVerify. [2]
4. Complete the live facial scan. [2]
5. Choose a partner bank. As of September 2026, the active partners are AUB and RCBC. SSS has signed agreements with China Bank, EastWest Rural Bank and UnionBank. [4]
6. Agree to share your data with the bank and submit. You will get a confirmation. [2]
7. Finish opening the bank account through the bank's app or a branch, and pay any bank fees. [2]
8. Wait for the card to be delivered. You do not need to visit an SSS branch for biometrics. [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/mysss-card/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): after you apply
content:
- The MySSS Card becomes your default account for SSS loans and benefits. [1]
- You can hold only one MySSS Card at a time. [2]
- Lost or damaged cards are replaced under the partner bank's rules. [1]
- Other government agencies are not required to accept the MySSS Card as their own membership card. [2]
- More than 400,000 MySSS Card accounts had been approved as of 30 July 2026. [4]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CI2025-008-External.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): background: what UMID was
content:
The Unified Multi-Purpose ID was created by Executive Order 420 (2005) to unify IDs across government agencies. The implementing rules named SSS, GSIS, Pag-IBIG and PhilHealth as participating agencies. [5] The old SSS rules on UMID cards (Circulars 2020-009 and 2021-011) were repealed by Circular 2025-008. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2005/eo_420_2005.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: MySSS Card (UMID replacement): problems and where to get help
content:
- The MySSS Card option is missing: check that your SS number is permanent and your contact details are complete. [1]
- National ID verification fails: make sure your name and date of birth match in SSS and PhilSys records. [2]
- Card delivery or account issues: contact your chosen partner bank. [1]
Help: SSS hotline 1455. Email [usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph](mailto:usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph). [6]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/CI2025-008-External.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PSA birth certificate: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Anyone who needs a PSA-issued copy of a birth certificate for school, work, a passport, benefits or court. You can request your own, your child's or your parent's, or one on behalf of the owner with authorisation. [3] [4]
Source: https://psahelpline.ph/faq (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: PSA birth certificate: fees
content:
What it costs: ₱155 per copy at a PSA Civil Registry System (CRS) outlet. [4] Online with home delivery: ₱330 through PSA Serbilis, or ₱365 through PSAHelpline. [1] [2] A view-only online copy is ₱130. [5]
Source: https://crs-appointment.psahelpline.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: PSA birth certificate: processing time
content:
How long it takes: At an outlet, about 1 hour if the record is in the database, or 7 working days if it is not. [4] Delivery in the Philippines takes about 3 to 9 working days through Serbilis, or the next working day in Metro Manila and 3 to 8 working days elsewhere through PSAHelpline. [1] [2]
Source: https://crs-appointment.psahelpline.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: PSA birth certificate: requirements
content:
- Write down the exact details as registered: full name, date and place of birth, and both parents' full names (mother's maiden name). [1]
- Prepare a valid ID for whoever will receive the document. [1] [4]
- Requesting for someone else at an outlet: bring the owner's ID, your own ID and an authorisation letter or SPA. A representative may request for at most 2 unrelated people. [4]
- Choose your channel: walk-in with appointment, PSA Serbilis delivery, PSAHelpline delivery, or view-only online copy.
Source: https://crs-itp2.psaserbilis.com.ph/Census/BirthCertificate (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: PSA birth certificate: steps: walk-in at a PSA CRS outlet
content:

title: Driver's license renewal: 5 or 10 years?
content:
Under RA 10930 (2017), licences are valid for 5 years, expiring on your birthday. On renewal, you get a 10-year licence only if you had no violations of the Land Transportation and Traffic Code or other traffic laws during the 5-year period. Otherwise you get another 5-year licence. [3] Under the LTO demerit-point system, 5 to 9 demerit points mean you must take the Driver's Reorientation Course. 10 to 39 points mean you also take a theoretical exam. [2]

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Employees who earn only salary (purely compensation income) and do not qualify for substituted filing. The most common case is having two or more employers in the same year (RR 4-2024).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%204-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): fees
content:
What it costs: Filing is free. You pay any income tax still due under the graduated rates (RA 10963 (TRAIN)).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2017/ra_10963_2017.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): do you need to file at all?
content:
You do not need to file Form 1700 if any of these apply (RR 4-2024):
- Your taxable compensation income is ₱250,000 or less.
- You had only one employer for the whole year and it withheld your tax correctly. This is "substituted filing": your employer's BIR Form 2316 stands in for your return.
- All of your income was already subject to final tax.
- You are a minimum wage earner.
- You are an overseas Filipino worker (OFW) for your income earned abroad.
You must file if you worked for two or more employers during the year, at the same time or one after another. RR 4-2024 says such earners "are not qualified for substituted filing" (RR 4-2024).
What is BIR Form 2316? It is the Certificate of Compensation Payment/Tax Withheld that your employer gives you. It shows what you earned and how much tax was withheld. Under substituted filing, it serves as your return. If you file Form 1700, you need one Form 2316 from each employer.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%204-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): requirements
content:
- Get a BIR Form 2316 from every employer you had during the year.
- Have your TIN and RDO code ready.
- Download the latest Offline eBIRForms package (v7.9.6.0 as of April 2026) from the BIR website (RMC 36-2026). Or log in to eFPS if you are enrolled (RMC 20-2026).
- Check you have a working email address. BIR sends your filing confirmation there (RMC 20-2026).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2036-2026.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): steps (part 1 of 2)
content:
1. Open eBIRForms and select 1700v2018 (RMC 20-2026).
2. Enter your background information (TIN, RDO, name, address).
3. Enter the compensation and tax withheld from each Form 2316.
4. Check the computed tax due against the graduated rates below.
5. Validate the form, then click Submit/Final Copy to file online (RR 4-2024 requires electronic filing unless the platforms are unavailable).
6. Screenshot the email confirmation pop-up and keep the confirmation email. These are your proof of filing; a "Received" stamp is not required (RMC 20-2026).
7. Pay any balance by the deadline. Use an ePay channel such as LANDBANK Link.BizPortal, UnionBank, or DBP PayTax/MyEG/Maya, or pay over the counter at an Authorized Agent Bank (RMC 20-2026). Revenue Collection Officers accept cash only up to ₱20,000 (RR 4-2024).
8. Submit any required attachments through the eAFS portal within 15 days after the deadline (RMC 20-2026).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%2020-2026.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): steps (part 2 of 2)
content:
If you need help, BIR eLounges prioritise employees with two or more employers and people filing for loans or travel (RMC 20-2026).

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): income tax rates (2023 onwards)
content:
Source: RA 10963 (TRAIN), Sec. 24(A)(2).

- Taxable income per year: ₱250,000 or less; Tax: 0%
- Taxable income per year: Over ₱250,000 to ₱400,000; Tax: 15% of the excess over ₱250,000
- Taxable income per year: Over ₱400,000 to ₱800,000; Tax: ₱22,500 + 20% of the excess over ₱400,000
- Taxable income per year: Over ₱800,000 to ₱2,000,000; Tax: ₱102,500 + 25% of the excess over ₱800,000
- Taxable income per year: Over ₱2,000,000 to ₱8,000,000; Tax: ₱402,500 + 30% of the excess over ₱2,000,000
- Taxable income per year: Over ₱8,000,000; Tax: ₱2,202,500 + 35% of the excess over ₱8,000,000
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2017/ra_10963_2017.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): deadlines and penalties
content:
- Deadline: 15 April of the following year (NIRC Sec. 51(C)(1)). BIR sometimes extends it. The 2025 returns were moved to 15 May 2026 (RMC 30-2026). The return for tax year 2026 falls due 15 April 2027 unless BIR announces otherwise.
- Where to file: Electronically, or at any Authorized Agent Bank, RDO or authorized software provider. You are no longer penalised for filing at the "wrong" RDO (RA 11976 (EOPT); RR 4-2024).
- Late filing or payment: A 25% surcharge applies (NIRC Sec. 248). Interest is charged at double the legal interest rate a year (TRAIN Sec. 249), which works out to 12%. Compromise penalties may also apply.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Annual ITR (BIR Form 1700): problems and where to get help
content:
- Two employers, but both withheld tax: You must still file Form 1700, because the combined income can push you into a higher bracket (RR 4-2024).
- No confirmation email: Do not refile right away. Check your spam folder, then contact BIR.
- You also have business or freelance income: Use Form 1701 (mixed income) instead of Form 1700.
- BIR Contact Center: (02) 8538-3200 and [contact_us@bir.gov.ph](mailto:contact_us@bir.gov.ph) (BIR Contact Us).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%204-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: BIR Form 1701A: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Self-employed people, freelancers, professionals and sole proprietors whose income comes purely from business or practice of a profession, and who either (a) use the graduated rates with the 40% Optional Standard Deduction (OSD), or (b) chose the 8% flat rate (RMC 17-2019). If you also have a salary, or you itemize deductions, use Form 1701 instead.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RMC%20No.%2017-2019.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: BIR Form 1701A: fees
content:
What it costs: Filing is free. Under the 8% option, the tax is 8% of gross sales or receipts and other non-operating income above ₱250,000. It replaces both the graduated income tax and the 3% percentage tax (TRAIN Sec. 24(A)(2)(b); RR 8-2018).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2017/ra_10963_2017.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: BIR Form 1701A: which rate are you on?
content:
- 8% flat rate: Only available if your gross sales/receipts plus other non-operating income do not exceed the ₱3,000,000 VAT threshold, and you are not VAT-registered (RR 8-2018).
- Choosing it: You must elect the 8% rate in your first-quarter income or percentage tax return, or in the first quarterly return after you start your business. Otherwise you are placed on graduated rates. The choice cannot be changed for that year (RR 8-2018).
- If you pass ₱3M during the year: You automatically move to graduated rates for the whole year. Your 8% quarterly payments are credited (RR 8-2018).
- Graduated rates + OSD: You deduct a flat 40% of gross sales/receipts instead of listing expenses (TRAIN Sec. 34(L)). You then pay graduated income tax plus 3% percentage tax if you are non-VAT (TRAIN Sec. 116).
- Micro and small taxpayers (gross sales below ₱3M is "micro") may instead use the simplified Form 1701-MS. It was added to eBIRForms v7.9.6.0 (RR 8-2024; RMC 20-2026; RMC 36-2026).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RR%20No.%208-2018.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: BIR Form 1701A: requirements
content:
- Confirm your Certificate of Registration lists Form 1701/1701A (or 1701-MS) and your chosen rate (RMC 20-2026).
- Total your gross sales/receipts for the year from your registered books and invoices.
- Gather your quarterly returns (1701Q) and proof of payment for the year.
- Collect BIR Form 2307 certificates from clients who withheld tax from your payments.
- Install the latest Offline eBIRForms package (v7.9.6.0 as of April 2026) (RMC 36-2026), or log in to eFPS if you are enrolled.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%2020-2026.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: BIR Form 1701A: steps (eBIRForms walkthrough)
content:
1. Open Offline eBIRForms and choose 1701A (RMC 20-2026).
2. Fill in your TIN, RDO code, name and business details.
3. Tick the tax regime you elected in the first quarter: "8%" or "graduated rates with OSD".
4. Enter your total gross sales/receipts and any other non-operating income.
5. Enter your quarterly payments and the creditable tax withheld shown on your 2307s.
6. Validate the return and correct any errors flagged.
7. Submit the return online and wait for the BIR confirmation email (RMC 20-2026).
8. Pay any balance through an ePay channel (LANDBANK Link.BizPortal, UnionBank, DBP PayTax/MyEG/Maya) or at an Authorized Agent Bank (RMC 20-2026).
9. Upload the required attachments (for example 2307s) through eAFS within 15 days after the deadline (RMC 20-2026). Under the 8% option, financial statements are not required (RR 8-2018). Under OSD, they are not required either (TRAIN Sec. 34(L)).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%2020-2026.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: BIR Form 1701A: deadlines and penalties
content:
- Return: 1701Q (Q1, Q2, Q3); Due: 15 May, 15 August, 15 November; Source: TRAIN Sec. 74
- Return: 1701A (annual); Due: 15 April of the following year (2025 returns: 15 May 2026); Source: NIRC Sec. 51; RMC 30-2026
- Return: 2551Q percentage tax (graduated-rate, non-VAT filers only); Due: Within 25 days after the end of each quarter; Source: EOPT Sec. 128

- Late filing or payment: 25% surcharge (NIRC Sec. 248), plus interest at double the legal rate, which is 12% a year (TRAIN Sec. 249).
- Micro and small taxpayers get lower penalties (RR 6-2024; EOPT Sec. 45):
	- 10% surcharge.
	- Interest at 50% of the regular rate (6%).
	- ₱500 per failure to file an information return, capped at ₱12,500 a year.
	- Compromise penalties cut by 50%.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2017/ra_10963_2017.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: BIR Form 1701A: problems and where to get help
content:
- I forgot to elect 8% in Q1. You are on graduated rates for the whole year, and the choice cannot be changed until next year (RR 8-2018).
- I also have a job. Use Form 1701 (mixed income), not 1701A (RMC 17-2019).
- I became VAT-registered. The 8% option is no longer available (RR 8-2018).

title: VAT registration: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: BIR-registered businesses and professionals who must register for VAT, plus anyone who chooses to register voluntarily. You must register if:
- Your gross sales for the past 12 months exceeded ₱3,000,000, or
- There are reasonable grounds to believe they will exceed ₱3,000,000 in the next 12 months.
Sources: EOPT Sec. 236(F); RR 3-2024.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_11976_2024.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: VAT registration: fees
content:
What it costs: BIR charges no registration fee. The ₱500 Annual Registration Fee ended on 22 Jan 2024 (RMC 14-2024). Once registered, you charge 12% VAT on your sales (RR 3-2024).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/RMC%20No.%2014-2024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: VAT registration: requirements
content:
- Add up your gross sales for the last 12 months, and estimate the next 12, excluding VAT-exempt sales (EOPT Sec. 236(F)).
- Download the October 2025 version of BIR Form 1905 (registration update) (RMC 97-2025).
- Check the document checklist for your type of business (RMC 74-2025).
- Know that the 8% income tax option ends once you register for VAT (RR 8-2018).
- If registering voluntarily, plan to stay VAT-registered for at least 3 years (EOPT Sec. 236(G)).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_11976_2024.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: VAT registration: steps
content:
1. Fill out BIR Form 1905 to add "Value-Added Tax" as a tax type (RMC 97-2025).
2. File it with your RDO, electronically (ORUS) or in person (EOPT Sec. 236).
3. Get your updated Certificate of Registration showing VAT. Pay ₱30 DST if a new COR is issued (RR 7-2024).
4. Apply for new invoices (Authority to Print, or a permit for loose-leaf or computerized invoices) that show VAT details (RR 7-2024). Each VAT invoice must show:
	- The words "VAT Reg TIN" followed by your TIN and branch code.
	- The VAT amount as a separate item.
5. Stop using your old non-VAT invoices.
6. Charge 12% VAT on every sale and issue an invoice for every sale, whatever the amount (RR 7-2024).
7. Record your sales and purchases separately so you can claim input VAT.
8. File BIR Form 2550Q (April 2024 version) and pay within 25 days after the end of each quarter (TRAIN/EOPT Sec. 114; RMC 68-2024).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2097-2025.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: VAT registration: what changes for your invoices and books
content:
- Invoices replace official receipts. Under EOPT, the "Invoice" is now the main sales document for both goods and services. An Official Receipt is only a supplementary document (RR 7-2024).
- Services are taxed on gross sales. VAT on services is now based on "gross sales", the same as goods, rather than on cash received (RR 3-2024).
- No more monthly 2550M. VAT returns are quarterly only, starting 1 January 2023. This change came from the TRAIN law, not EOPT (RA 10963 Sec. 114).
- Threshold will be updated. The ₱3M threshold is adjusted for inflation every 3 years (EOPT Sec. 109(CC); RR 3-2024). Check current BIR issuances when determining whether you must register.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: VAT registration: deadlines and penalties
content:
- If you should have registered but didn't: You must pay VAT as if registered, but you cannot claim input tax credits for that period (EOPT Sec. 236(F)(2)).
- Registration deadline: Contact your RDO as soon as your sales reach the registration threshold to confirm when you must file your registration update.
- Late filing or payment:
	- 25% surcharge (NIRC Sec. 248).
	- 12% a year interest (TRAIN Sec. 249).
	- Micro and small taxpayers pay a reduced 10% surcharge and 6% interest instead (RR 6-2024).
- Cancelling VAT registration: Possible if you expect sales over the next 12 months to stay at or below the threshold, or if you close the business. The cancellation takes effect on the first day of the following month (EOPT Sec. 236(E)(2)).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_11976_2024.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: VAT registration: problems and where to get help
content:
- "My old receipts say Official Receipt." The transition period ended on 31 December 2024. Issuing an "Official Receipt" for sales after 30 June 2024 is penalised (RR 7-2024).
- "I'm on 8% and crossed ₱3M." You are moved to graduated rates for the year and must register for VAT (RR 8-2018).
- BIR Contact Center: (02) 8538-3200 and [contact_us@bir.gov.ph](mailto:contact_us@bir.gov.ph) (BIR Contact Us).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Every Filipino citizen is automatically covered by the National Health Insurance Program under the Universal Health Care Act (RA 11223). You register to get a PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN) and to pay contributions if you are a direct contributor. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: fees
content:
What it costs: Registration is free. Direct contributors pay 5% of monthly basic income, effective January 2025. The minimum is ₱500 a month, for incomes up to ₱10,000, and the maximum is ₱5,000 a month, for incomes of ₱100,000 and up. [2] [1] Employees pay half and employers pay half. [4]
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2026/PA2026-0042.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: processing time
content:
How long it takes: Online PIN applications are processed in 3 to 5 working days, and the PIN is sent by email. [5]
Source: https://memberinquiry.philhealth.gov.ph/member/pinApplication.xhtml (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: member types
content:
- Direct contributors pay premiums themselves or with their employer. They include employees, self-earning people, professionals, OFWs, migrant workers, Filipinos with dual citizenship, and lifetime members. [1]
- Indirect contributors have premiums paid by the government. They include indigents, 4Ps beneficiaries, senior citizens, PWDs, Sangguniang Kabataan officials and others under the law. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: requirements
content:
- Download and fill in the PhilHealth Member Registration Form (PMRF). [6]
- Prepare your PSA birth certificate or a valid ID. Online applications need a scan. [5]
- List your dependents with their birth or marriage certificates, if you are declaring any. [6]
- Use an email address that has not been used for another PIN application. Only one application is allowed per email. [5]
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/downloads/membership/pmrf_012020.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: steps: online
content:
1. Open the PhilHealth PIN application page. [5]
2. Enter your details as they appear on your PMRF. [5]
3. Upload your birth certificate or valid ID. [5]
4. Submit, and wait 3 to 5 working days for your PIN by email. [5]
Source: https://memberinquiry.philhealth.gov.ph/member/pinApplication.xhtml (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: steps: employees
content:
1. Give two completed PMRF copies to your employer's HR. [4]
2. Check that your employer reports you and deducts your half of the premium from your pay. [4]
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/members/formal/registration.php (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: steps: self-earning, voluntary or informal-sector members
content:
1. Bring two PMRF copies and your supporting document to a Local Health Insurance Office (LHIO) or PhilHealth Express. [3]
2. Receive your PIN and Member Data Record (MDR). [3]
3. Pay your first premium monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or annually through PhilHealth, accredited collecting agents, the Member Portal or the eGov PH app. [2]
4. Pay on time: the deadline is the last working day of the month or quarter you are paying for. [3]
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/members/informal/registration.php (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: after you apply
content:
- Eligibility is immediate. You do not need a PhilHealth ID card to use benefits. [1]
- Missed contributions: direct contributors pay them with interest. The law sets at least 3% per month for employers, and up to 1.5% per month for self-earning members. [1]
- Example contributions: ₱10,000 income → ₱500; ₱30,000 → ₱1,500; ₱100,000 → ₱5,000 a month. [2]
- Rate history: the 5% rate was set for 2024–2025 in RA 11223. [1] In 2023, the scheduled increase was suspended and the rate stayed at 4%, with an ₱80,000 income ceiling. [7] The 5% rate took effect in January 2025, and PhilHealth's July 2026 advisory still applies it. [2]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11223_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: PhilHealth registration: problems and where to get help
content:
- Duplicate PINs: do not register twice. Ask an LHIO to merge duplicate records.
- Employer not remitting: check your contributions in the Member Portal, then report it to PhilHealth. [2]
Help: PhilHealth Action Center (02) 8662-2588, [actioncenter@philhealth.gov.ph](mailto:actioncenter@philhealth.gov.ph). [2]
Source: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2026/PA2026-0042.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: SSS pension claim: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: SSS members retiring or with a disability, and the beneficiaries of a member who has died.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11199_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: fees
content:
What it costs: Filing is free.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11199_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

title: SSS pension claim: how much you get
content:
- Minimum monthly pension: ₱1,200 with at least 10 credited years of service, or ₱2,400 with at least 20 credited years. [1]
- Dependent's pension: 10% of your monthly pension or ₱250, whichever is higher, for each minor child, up to 5 children. [1]
- 13th-month pension: paid every December. [2]
- Lump-sum option: retirees may take the first 18 months as a discounted lump sum. [1]
- Pension increases: the Pension Reform Program raises pensions every September from 2025 to 2027. The second increase was moved up to June 2026: +10% for retirement and disability pensioners, +5% for death and survivor pensioners. [6]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11199_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: requirements
content:
- Register for My.SSS at member.sss.gov.ph. [2]
- Set up a disbursement account, such as a MySSS Card, UMID-ATM, or bank or e-wallet account approved through the Disbursement Account Enrollment Module (DAEM). The MySSS Card automatically becomes your default account. [2] [7]
- Retiring at 60 to 64: get a certificate of separation from your employer, or an affidavit that you have stopped self-employment. [2]
- Disability: get the SSS Medical Certificate completed by your doctor (issued within 6 months), plus your medical records. [3]
- Death: get the member's PSA death certificate, your PSA marriage certificate (spouse) and the children's PSA birth certificates. [4]
- Representative filing: get a Letter of Authority or SPA dated within 6 months (Philippines) or 1 year (abroad). [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/retirement-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: steps: retirement (online)
content:
1. Log in to My.SSS. [2]
2. Apply for retirement benefits through My.SSS. [2]
3. Choose your disbursement account and pension option (monthly, or 18-month advance plus monthly). [2]
4. Upload any required documents, then submit. [2]
5. Watch your email and My.SSS for the claim status. [2]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/retirement-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: steps: disability
content:
1. File the disability claim at any SSS branch within 10 years of the disability. Bring the SSS Medical Certificate, completed by your doctor within 6 months of filing. [3]
2. Attend the evaluation or physical examination by an SSS medical specialist, if scheduled. [3]
3. Submit the Annual Confirmation of Pensioners (ACOP) when required, to keep your pension active. [3]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/disability-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: steps: death and survivor pension
content:
1. Identify the beneficiaries. Primary beneficiaries are the dependent spouse and dependent children under 21. If there are none, the secondary beneficiaries are the dependent parents. [4]
2. File over the counter at any SSS branch. A qualified dependent legal spouse with an SS number and a My.SSS account may file online, under Circular 2022-009. [4]
3. Submit the death, marriage and birth certificates and IDs. [4]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/death-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SSS pension claim: after you apply
content:
- Pensions are credited monthly to your disbursement account. [2]
- Disability pensioners who fail to appear for the yearly Annual Confirmation of Pensioners (ACOP) examination have their pension suspended. The pension is cancelled if they return to work or recover. [3]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/retirement-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

title: SSS pension claim: problems and where to get help
content:
- No disbursement account on file: enrol one in My.SSS (DAEM) before filing. [2]
- Retirement claims that must be filed at a branch: these include members with outstanding SILP, privatization, educational or vocational loans, members with dependent children under guardianship, incapacitated members, members covered by portability law or bilateral agreements, and claims for re-adjudication. [2]
Help: SSS hotline 1455. Email [usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph](mailto:usssaptayo@sss.gov.ph). [5]
Source: https://www.sss.gov.ph/retirement-benefit/ (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Pag-IBIG membership: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Coverage is mandatory for employees covered by SSS or GSIS, self-employed people, OFWs, uniformed personnel, kasambahays and other earning groups. People aged 18 to 65 can join voluntarily, including non-working spouses. [1] [2]
Source: https://mpm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/HDMF-Circular-No.-460-Pag-ibig-HDMF-Table-2024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Pag-IBIG membership: fees
content:
What it costs: Registration is free. Monthly savings are 2% of your monthly fund salary from you and 2% from your employer, or 1% from you if you earn ₱1,500 or less. The fund salary is capped at ₱10,000 since February 2024, so the most required is ₱200 from you and ₱200 from your employer. You may save more. Self-employed members pay both shares. [1]
Source: https://mpm.ph/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/HDMF-Circular-No.-460-Pag-ibig-HDMF-Table-2024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Pag-IBIG membership: what the MID number is
content:
The Pag-IBIG Membership ID (MID) number is your permanent Pag-IBIG account number. You use it for remitting contributions, creating a Virtual Pag-IBIG account, and applying for loans. [3]
Source: https://www.pagibigfundservices.com/virtualpagibig/FAQs.aspx (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Pag-IBIG membership: requirements
content:
- Prepare a working mobile number for the one-time PIN (OTP) and an email address. [3]
- Get your passport or two valid primary IDs, and be ready to take a selfie for account verification. [3]
- Check that your employer details (employer ID) are available, if you are employed.
Source: https://www.pagibigfundservices.com/virtualpagibig/FAQs.aspx (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Pag-IBIG membership: steps
content:
1. Go to Pag-IBIG online membership registration. [4]
2. Fill in your personal, address and employment details, then submit to get a Registration Tracking Number (RTN). [4]
3. Get your permanent MID number. [3]
4. Create a Virtual Pag-IBIG account with your MID, name, birth date and mobile number, then verify with the OTP. [3]
5. Upload your ID and selfie to complete verification. [3]
6. Give your MID to your employer so it can remit your contributions, or pay your own contributions if you are self-employed or a voluntary member. [1]
Source: https://www.pagibigfundservices.com/OnlineMembershipRegistration (checked 2026-10-09).

title: Pag-IBIG membership: after you apply
content:
- Membership term: your savings mature after 20 years, with 240 monthly contributions. [2]
- Employer share: your employer must match its share and may not deduct it from your wages. [1] [2]
- Housing loan: Before applying, confirm your eligibility, contribution requirements and loan terms with Pag-IBIG.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2009/ra_9679_2009.html (checked 2026-10-09).

- Contributions not posted: check your records in Virtual Pag-IBIG, then ask your employer for proof of remittance. [3]

title: DTI business name registration: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Filipinos aged 18 or older who will run a business alone under a business name. Foreign nationals, recognised refugees and stateless persons must also go to a DTI office with extra documents (DTI BNRS FAQ; BNRS Registration Guide).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: DTI business name registration: fees
content:
What it costs: ₱200 (barangay), ₱500 (city/municipality), ₱1,000 (regional) or ₱2,000 (national), plus ₱30 documentary stamp tax (DTI BNRS FAQ).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: DTI business name registration: processing time
content:
How long it takes: Online. Your certificate is emailed once payment goes through (BNRS Registration Guide). You must pay within 7 calendar days of applying (BNRS Registration Guide).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/resources/registration-guide (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: DTI business name registration: requirements
content:
- Pick your territorial scope: barangay, city/municipality, region or national. It sets your fee and where you may operate under that name (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- Prepare a business name with a "dominant name" plus a "descriptor" for what you do, for example "Liwanag Bakery" (BNRS Registration Guide).
- Avoid words like "Corporation", "Company" or "Incorporated". These are for SEC-registered entities (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- Have a valid ID and an email address you can access. Your certificate and verification codes are sent there (BNRS Registration Guide).
- Get an e-wallet, card or Landbank Link.Biz ready for payment (BNRS Registration Guide).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: DTI business name registration: steps
content:
1. Go to bnrs.dti.gov.ph, choose New Registration and click "I Agree" (BNRS Registration Guide).
2. Fill out the owner's information and confirm it.
3. Select your territorial scope and enter your dominant name and descriptor.
4. Click Check Name Availability. If the name is taken, try another.
5. Write down your Reference Code. You will need it for every later transaction.
6. Fill out your business address, personal information, residence and other details.
7. Review the summary and confirm it, then agree to the Undertaking.
8. Pay the fee within 7 calendar days using DTI Teller, GCash, Maya, Landbank Link.Biz or a card. If you do not pay in time, the application is deemed abandoned and nullified (BNRS Registration Guide).
9. Download your Certificate of Business Name Registration. You can also get it later through Transaction Inquiry with your Reference Code and an email verification code (DTI BNRS FAQ).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: DTI business name registration: after you apply
content:
- The DTI certificate is not a business permit. You still need a Mayor's Permit from your city or municipality (DTI BNRS FAQ). See the Mayor's Permit guide.
- Register with BIR. Do this on or before you start doing business, meaning your first sale or 30 days after your DTI registration or Mayor's Permit, whichever comes first (RR 7-2024).
- Validity: 5 years from registration (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- Renewal windows (DTI BNRS FAQ):
	- Early: up to 180 days before expiry.
	- Regular: within 90 days after expiry.
	- Grace: a further 90 days, with a 50% surcharge on the registration fee.
- Ownership cannot be transferred. A new owner must register a new business name (DTI BNRS FAQ).
Source: https://bnrs.dti.gov.ph/faq (checked 2026-10-09).

title: DTI business name registration: problems and where to get help
content:
- Typo in your registration: Only typographical errors in new registrations can be corrected. Email the helpdesk with your name, business name, the correction and a government ID (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- Moving outside your scope: If you move or expand beyond your territorial scope, change your scope. This is treated as a new application (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- Applying through someone else: A representative may file with a valid ID and an authorization letter from the owner (DTI BNRS FAQ).
- BNRS Helpdesk (BNRS):
	- Email: [bnrshelpdesk@dtiphmail.dti.gov.ph](mailto:bnrshelpdesk@dtiphmail.dti.gov.ph).
	- Text/Viber: 0917-595-3930.
	- Calls: 0917-863-0669 / 0917-845-7104.

title: SEC corporation registration: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: People forming a stock corporation (2 to 15 incorporators), a One Person Corporation (OPC), a non-stock corporation, or a partnership with the Securities and Exchange Commission (RA 11232 Sec. 10; SEC eSPARC).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11232_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SEC corporation registration: fees
content:
What it costs: The filing fee for the Articles of Incorporation is 1/5 of 1% of authorized capital stock, or of the subscription price if higher, with a minimum of ₱2,000. Add a 1% legal research fee (minimum ₱10), the by-laws fee and other small fees (SEC MC 3 s.2017; SEC Registration Fee Calculator). No minimum capital is required unless a special law says otherwise (RA 11232 Secs. 12 and 117).
Source: https://appointment.sec.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2017MCno03-new2.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SEC corporation registration: processing time
content:
How long it takes: Under Regular Processing, SEC emails the review result within 7 working days (SEC eSPARC).
Source: https://esparc.sec.gov.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SEC corporation registration: requirements
content:
- Decide the type: a regular stock corporation (2 to 15 incorporators) or an OPC (a single stockholder who is a natural person, trust or estate) (RA 11232 Secs. 10 and 116).
- Choose a company name. An OPC must add "OPC" to its name (RA 11232 Sec. 120).
- Decide your authorized capital stock and subscriptions. These set your fees (SEC Registration Fee Calculator).
- For an OPC, name a nominee and an alternate nominee and get their written consent (RA 11232 Sec. 124).
- Choose a processing option on eSPARC: OneSEC, Regular, or ZERO (Zuper Easy Registration Online, which uses digital signing so nothing is sent on paper) (SEC eSPARC).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2019/ra_11232_2019.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SEC corporation registration: steps (Regular Processing)
content:
1. Open esparc.sec.gov.ph and choose Regular Processing for your company type (SEC eSPARC).
2. Submit your proposed company name.
3. Enter the Articles of Incorporation and By-laws details.
4. Wait for SEC's email on the review status, sent within 7 working days. If SEC sends a compliance notice, correct the data and resubmit (SEC eSPARC).
5. Pay the fees on the Payment Assessment Form through eSPAYSEC or Landbank over the counter (SEC eSPARC).
6. Receive your Certificate of Incorporation.
7. Send two hard copies of the signed and notarized documents with your proof of payment to SEC by courier or registered mail. Do this within 60 calendar days of the approval date on the certificate (SEC eSPARC).
8. Get your corporate TIN and SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG employer numbers through the Philippine Business Hub, which eSPARC links to (SEC eSPARC).
Source: https://esparc.sec.gov.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: SEC corporation registration: after you apply
content:
- Business permit and BIR: Get your Mayor's Permit, then register with BIR on or before starting operations. That means your first sale or 30 days after SEC registration, whichever comes first (RR 7-2024).
- OPC officers: Appoint a treasurer and corporate secretary within 15 days of incorporation, and notify SEC within 5 days of their appointment (RA 11232 Sec. 122). Check with SEC for the required appointment forms and submission instructions.
- Single stockholder as treasurer: Check with SEC about the bond and filing requirements if the single stockholder will also serve as treasurer.
- Annual reports: File the General Information Sheet and audited financial statements through SEC eFAST (SEC eFAST list of reportorial requirements).
- Term: A corporation exists perpetually unless its articles say otherwise (RA 11232 Sec. 11).
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

title: SEC corporation registration: problems and where to get help
content:
- Application disapproved: Edit the fields named in the compliance notice and resubmit, or cancel and re-apply (SEC eSPARC).
- Hard-copy submission deadline: If you cannot meet the 60-day deadline, contact the SEC registration office for guidance.
- OPC representative: For BIR registration, an OPC representative needs a Written Resolution; a Special Power of Attorney is not accepted (RMC 74-2025).
- SEC registration help: [cprd_registration@sec.gov.ph](mailto:cprd_registration@sec.gov.ph) (SEC eSPARC).

title: Mayor's permit: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Anyone opening or renewing a business in a Philippine city or municipality: sole proprietors (DTI), corporations and partnerships (SEC), and cooperatives (CDA).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11032_2018.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: fees
content:
What it costs: It varies by LGU. Your bill includes local business tax, which is usually based on capital for new businesses and gross sales for renewals, plus regulatory fees set by your city's revenue code. Quezon City, for example, taxes new businesses on declared capitalization (QC BPLD Citizen's Charter 2026). The fire safety inspection fee is 15% of the fees the LGU charges, with a minimum of ₱500 (BFP MC 2021-020).
Source: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/BPLD_2026-CC.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: processing time
content:
How long it takes: By law, no more than 3 working days for simple, 7 for complex, and 20 for highly technical or high-risk applications (RA 11032 Sec. 9). Quezon City estimates 1 to 3 days (QC guide).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11032_2018.html (checked 2026-10-09).
