title: Mayor's permit: how the process works now
content:
Under the Ease of Doing Business Act, you no longer go office by office. Every city and municipality must (RA 11032 Sec. 11):
- Use one unified application form. It covers local taxes, building, sanitary, zoning and other clearances, including the BFP fire clearance.
- Process it at a Business One-Stop Shop (BOSS), in person or online (e-BOSS).
- Handle barangay clearance at the city or municipal level.
- Issue sanitary and other local clearances together with the permit.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11032_2018.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: requirements
content:
- Register your business name with DTI, or your company with SEC or CDA (QC guide).
- Prepare proof of your business location: a tax declaration or title if you own it, or a notarized lease if you rent (QC guide).
- Take photos of the location, or draw a sketch, as your LGU requires (QC guide).
- Have the owner's valid ID ready (QC guide).
- If your building already has an occupancy-stage Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC), get a copy. It can serve as the basis for your business FSIC (RA 11032 Sec. 12).
- Check your city or municipality's own BOSS page for any extra requirements.
Source: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/opening-a-business-in-qc/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: steps (worked example: Quezon City online)
content:
1. Create an account on QC E-Services (QC guide).
2. Go to Business One-Stop Shop and choose "Apply for Mayor's Permit (Business)".
3. Fill out the Unified Application Form.
4. Upload your ID, DTI/SEC/CDA registration, proof of location and photos.
5. Wait for your risk classification and assessment. QC classifies new permits as low risk (3 working days), medium (7) or high (20). Renewals take 3 days (QC EO 38 s.2025; QC BPLD Citizen's Charter 2026).
6. Pay the tax bill online or at the treasury.
7. Download or claim your Mayor's Permit.
8. Prepare for inspections. In QC, these happen after the permit is issued, except the fire safety (FSIC) inspection (QC EO 38 s.2025).
9. Register with BIR on or before you start operating. That means your first sale, or 30 days after your Mayor's Permit or DTI/SEC registration, whichever comes first (RR 7-2024).
Other LGUs follow the same legal framework, but their portals and fees differ.
Source: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/opening-a-business-in-qc/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: deadlines, renewals and penalties
content:
- Validity: A business permit is valid for 1 year. Your LGU renews either in January or on the anniversary of issuance (RA 11032 Sec. 11(e)).
- Paying business tax: Local business taxes are due within the first 20 days of January, or of each quarter if paid quarterly (RA 7160 Sec. 167).
- Late payment: LGUs may charge a surcharge of up to 25%, plus interest of up to 2% a month for at most 36 months (RA 7160 Sec. 168). The actual rates are in your local revenue code.
- Fire safety certificate (renewals): BFP must give your LGU the FSIC within 3 working days. If it does not, you are deemed to hold a temporary valid FSIC and your permit is renewed automatically. Tell BFP about any renovations 30 working days before the permit expires (RA 11032 Sec. 12).
- If the office doesn't act in time: An application that is complete but not acted on within the processing time is deemed approved (RA 11032, new Sec. 10 of RA 9485).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11032_2018.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Mayor's permit: problems and where to get help
content:
- Asked to submit the same document twice: The business permit office may not require documents you already gave other LGU departments, such as a barangay clearance (RA 11032, new Sec. 14 of RA 9485).
- Fire extinguisher brand "required": BFP staff may not sell or recommend specific brands (RA 11032 Sec. 12(f)).
- Quezon City BPLD: [bpld@quezoncity.gov.ph](mailto:bpld@quezoncity.gov.ph), 8988-4242 loc. 8173 (QC guide).
- Red tape complaints: 8888 Citizens' Complaint Center; Contact Center ng Bayan 1-6565; ARTA at [complaints@arta.gov.ph](mailto:complaints@arta.gov.ph) (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024, contact annex).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11032_2018.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Buyers and sellers of titled land, or of a house and lot, held as a capital asset (not by a real-estate dealer) who need a new Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) in the buyer's name.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: fees
content:
What it costs: >
- Capital gains tax (CGT): 6% (NIRC Sec. 24(D); still 6% after CMEPA per RR 21-2025).
- Documentary stamp tax (DST): 1.5%, or ₱15 per ₱1,000 (NIRC Sec. 196).
- Transfer tax: up to 0.5% in provinces, or up to 0.75% in cities and Metro Manila municipalities (RA 7160 Secs. 135 and 151).
- eCAR: ₱100 certification fee + ₱30 DST (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- Registry of Deeds registration fees (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: processing time
content:
How long it takes: >
- BIR eCAR: about 7 working days after a complete filing (RMC 28-2025).
- Registry of Deeds new title: 19 working days, 2 hours and 35 minutes (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024).
- Plus time for the notary and the LGU treasurer.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2028-2025.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: how the taxes are computed (part 1 of 2)
content:
- Tax: CGT (BIR Form 1706). By law, a tax on the seller.; Rate and base: 6% of the gross selling price or fair market value, whichever is higher; Deadline: Within 30 days from notarization of the deed; Source: NIRC Secs. 24(D), 51(C)(2)(b); RMC 75-2026
- Tax: DST (BIR Form 2000-OT); Rate and base: ₱15 per ₱1,000 (1.5%) of the consideration or fair market value, whichever is higher; Deadline: Within 5 days after the end of the month the deed was notarized; Source: NIRC Sec. 196; RMC 75-2026
- Tax: Local transfer tax; Rate and base: Up to 0.5% (provinces) or 0.75% (cities and Metro Manila municipalities) of the consideration or fair market value, whichever is higher; Deadline: Within 60 days from execution of the deed; Source: RA 7160 Secs. 135, 151

- Fair market value: BIR zonal values remain in force until the new Schedule of Market Values (SMV) under the Real Property Valuation and Assessment Reform Act takes over. That Act also amends the tax bases in NIRC Sec. 24(D) and LGC Sec. 135(a) (RA 12001 Secs. 31, 38).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: how the taxes are computed (part 2 of 2)
content:
- Selling your principal residence: It may be exempt from CGT if you use the proceeds to buy or build a new principal residence within 18 months (NIRC Sec. 24(D)(2)).
- Ordinary assets (property used in business, or held by dealers) do not pay CGT. They are subject to creditable withholding tax, filed on BIR Form 1606 by the 10th of the following month (RMC 75-2026).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: requirements
content:
- Make sure both parties have TINs. A one-time taxpayer can get one with BIR Form 1904 (RR 7-2024).
- Get a certified true copy of the title from the Registry of Deeds (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- Get a certified true copy of the latest tax declaration from the Assessor (BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
- Pay all real property tax and get a realty tax clearance (LRA Circular 10-2020).
- Keep the owner's duplicate copy of the title safe. The Registry of Deeds needs it (LRA Circular 10-2020).
- Agree in writing who will pay which tax and fee.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RR%20No.%207-%202024.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: steps (part 1 of 2)
content:
1. Sign the Deed of Absolute Sale (DOAS) and have it notarized. The notarization date starts the BIR deadlines (RMC 75-2026).
2. File and pay the CGT (Form 1706) within 30 days of notarization (RMC 75-2026).
3. File and pay the DST (Form 2000-OT) within 5 days after the end of the notarization month (RMC 75-2026).
4. Submit the ONETT documents to the BIR RDO where the property is located. These include the notarized DOAS, the certified title, the certified tax declaration, the TIN verification and proof of tax payments (RMC 75-2026; BIR Citizen's Charter 2025).
5. Claim the electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR). BIR will also stamp every page of the deed. An eCAR from the eCAR System stays valid until it is presented to the Registry of Deeds; no revalidation is needed (RR 12-2024; LRA Circular 10-2020).
6. Pay the transfer tax at the provincial or city treasurer within 60 days of the deed (RA 7160 Sec. 135).
7. File at the Registry of Deeds. Bring the following (LRA Circular 10-2020):
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2075-2026_Redacted.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: steps (part 2 of 2)
content:
- The BIR-stamped deed.
	- The eCAR.
	- The owner's duplicate title.
	- The certified tax declaration.
	- The realty tax clearance.
	- The transfer tax receipt.
8. Pay the Registry of Deeds fees (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024):
	- ₱30 entry fee.
	- Registration fee, based on value.
	- ₱344.93 IT fee per deed.
	- ₱60 per owner's duplicate title, plus a ₱215.58 IT fee per title.
	- ₱30 per annotation, including the eCAR annotation.
	- Legal research fee: 1% of the registration fee, minimum ₱10.
9. Claim the new TCT in the buyer's name.
10. Bring the new title to the city or municipal Assessor to transfer the tax declaration to the new owner. Ask the Assessor for the local document checklist.
Source: https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/BIR/pdf/RMC%20No.%2075-2026_Redacted.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: deadlines and penalties
content:
- Late CGT, DST or 1606: A 25% surcharge applies (NIRC Sec. 248), plus interest at 12% a year, which is double the legal rate (TRAIN Sec. 249).
- Late transfer tax: Surcharge and interest follow the local revenue code, within the caps in RA 7160 Sec. 168 (up to 25%, plus up to 2% a month for at most 36 months).
- eCAR processing:
	- One-time transaction case: 3 working days (simple) or 7 (complex) (RMC 28-2025).
	- eCAR issuance: 7 working days (RMC 28-2025).
- Filing method: Returns are filed electronically, or manually if the electronic platforms are unavailable (RMC 75-2026).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1997/ra_8424_1997.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Land title transfer: problems and where to get help
content:
- Registry of Deeds fee: Ask your Registry of Deeds for a fee assessment before payment.
- Lost owner's duplicate title: Contact the Registry of Deeds for guidance on replacing the lost owner's duplicate before proceeding with a transfer.
- BIR: (02) 8538-3200, [contact_us@bir.gov.ph](mailto:contact_us@bir.gov.ph) (BIR Contact Us).
- LRA Public Relations and Information Section: [pris@lra.gov.ph](mailto:pris@lra.gov.ph), 0927-631-1949 (Globe), 0960-465-5340 (Smart) (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024).
- Complaints: 8888 Citizens' Complaint Center; ARTA at [complaints@arta.gov.ph](mailto:complaints@arta.gov.ph) (LRA Citizen's Charter 2024).
Source: https://www.bir.gov.ph/contactus (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Owners, and anyone with beneficial use, of land, buildings or machinery in the Philippines.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): fees
content:
What it costs: Your LGU sets the rate within these legal caps (RA 7160 Secs. 233, 235):
- Basic real property tax: up to 1% of assessed value in provinces, or up to 2% in cities and Metro Manila municipalities.
- Special Education Fund levy: 1% on top.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): processing time
content:
How long it takes: Minutes online if your LGU has an e-payment portal. Quezon City sends the official receipt in 2 to 3 business days (QC how-to).
Source: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/how-to-pay-your-real-property-tax/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): when to pay
content:
- When it becomes due: The tax for the year accrues on 1 January (RA 7160 Sec. 246).
- Paying in instalments: Pay in four quarterly instalments, due by 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December (RA 7160 Sec. 250).
- Early-payment discount: Your sanggunian may grant a discount of up to 20% for advance or prompt payment (RA 7160 Sec. 251). Example: Quezon City gave the following discounts for 2026 RPT (QC RPT schedule, 15 Jan 2026):
	- 20% if paid in full by 31 Dec 2025.
	- 10% if paid in full from 1 Jan to 31 Mar 2026.
	- No discount for quarterly payment.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): requirements
content:
- Find your Tax Declaration Number (TDN) or Property Index Number on your tax declaration or last receipt (QC how-to).
- Check your LGU's current rates and discount schedule. They are set by local ordinance.
- Choose a payment channel: City or Municipal Treasurer, a branch office, or the LGU's online portal.
- If you recently bought the property, make sure the tax declaration has been moved to your name.
Source: https://quezoncity.gov.ph/qcitizen-guides/how-to-pay-your-real-property-tax/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): steps (worked example: Quezon City online)
content:
1. Log in to QC E-Services (QC RPT schedule).
2. Choose Real Property Tax and enter your TDN (QC how-to).
3. Review the billing, including any back taxes, and choose to pay annually or quarterly.
4. Pay with GCash, Maya, a credit or debit card, Landbank or UnionBank (QC RPT schedule).
5. Save the payment confirmation, and wait 2 to 3 business days for the official receipt (QC how-to).
6. Keep your receipts. You will need a realty tax clearance when you sell or transfer the property (LRA Circular 10-2020).
In other LGUs, go to the City or Municipal Treasurer's Office with your TDN or last receipt, or use the LGU's own e-payment portal.
Source: https://qceservices.quezoncity.gov.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): penalties if you miss a payment
content:
- Interest: Unpaid RPT earns interest of 2% a month, for a maximum of 36 months, so up to 72% of the unpaid amount (RA 7160 Sec. 255). Interest runs on each missed instalment, not only after a whole year.
- Collection: The LGU can levy the property, sell it at public auction, and take other collection action (RA 7160 Secs. 256 to 258).
- Disputing the bill: Pay the tax "under protest" first, then file a written protest with the treasurer within 30 days of payment (RA 7160 Sec. 252).
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): recent changes (RA 12001, Real Property Valuation and Assessment Reform Act)
content:
- Effective date: 5 July 2024 (RA 12001).
- Cap on increases: In the first year a new Schedule of Market Values (SMV) is used, any RPT increase is capped at 6% (RA 12001 Sec. 29).
- Amnesty: Penalties and interest on RPT unpaid before the Act took effect could be waived if paid within 2 years, that is by 5 July 2026 (RA 12001 Sec. 30; BLGF MC 001-2025 (IRR)). Ask your local treasurer about any amnesty currently available and its payment deadline.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_12001_2024.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Real property tax (amilyar): problems and where to get help
content:
- "I didn't get a bill." RPT is still due without a bill. The due dates are set by law (RA 7160 Sec. 250).
- Paid online but no receipt: In QC, email [rptpayment@quezoncity.gov.ph](mailto:rptpayment@quezoncity.gov.ph) (QC how-to).
- Quezon City Treasurer's Office (QC RPT schedule):
	- Phone: 8988-4242 loc. 8317, 8145, 8156 or 8157.
	- Email: [CTO@quezoncity.gov.ph](mailto:CTO@quezoncity.gov.ph).
	- QC Helpline: 122.
- Elsewhere: Contact your City or Municipal Treasurer's Office, or the Provincial Treasurer for municipalities outside Metro Manila.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1991/ra_7160_1991.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: Couples marrying in the Philippines, in a civil or religious ceremony. Both of you must be at least 18. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: fees
content:
What it costs: Each city or municipality sets its own fees. For example, Legazpi City charges ₱300 for the application, ₱200 for the licence, and ₱100 for family planning. [4] Indigent couples are exempt from licence fees under the Family Code. [1] PSA copies of supporting documents cost extra; see the CENOMAR and birth certificate guides.
Source: https://legazpi.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/REVISED-CITIZEN-CHARTER-2025-A3.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: processing time
content:
How long it takes: At least 10 consecutive days, the required posting period for the application, before the licence can be issued. [1] Once issued, the licence is valid anywhere in the Philippines for 120 days. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: requirements
content:
- Find the Local Civil Registrar (LCR) of the city or municipality where either of you usually lives. You apply there. [1]
- Get PSA birth certificates for both partners. [1] [4]
- Get PSA CENOMARs for both partners, if your LCR requires them. Legazpi does, for example. [4]
- Prepare valid IDs for both partners. [4]
- Ages 18 to 20: get written parental consent. [1]
- Ages 21 to 24: ask for parental advice. If advice is refused or not obtained, the licence is delayed by 3 months. [1]
- Previously married: get the death certificate of your late spouse, or the court decree of annulment or nullity. [1]
- Foreign partner: get a certificate of legal capacity to marry from their embassy or consulate. [1]
- Religious wedding: ask your church about its own requirements, such as Pre-Cana seminars, baptismal and confirmation certificates. These are church rules, not civil law.
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: steps (part 1 of 2)
content:
1. Attend the family planning and responsible parenthood session at your local health or family planning office, and get the Certificate of Compliance. RA 10354 says this certificate is required before the licence is issued and is free of charge. [2]
2. If either of you needed parental consent or advice, complete marriage counselling and get the certificate. Without it, the licence is delayed by 3 months. [1]
3. Appear together at the LCR to file the marriage licence application under oath. [1] [4]
4. Pay the LGU fees. [4]
5. Wait for the 10-day posting period to end. [1]
6. Claim the marriage licence. [1]
7. Hold the ceremony within 120 days. You need an authorised solemnising officer: a judge, priest, rabbi, imam or minister of a registered church, a ship captain or military commander in specific cases, a consul abroad, or a city or municipal mayor. You also need at least two witnesses aged 18 or over. [1] [3]
8. Sign the marriage certificate with your officer and witnesses. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10354_2012.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: steps (part 2 of 2)
content:
9. Confirm that the solemnising officer sends the marriage certificate to the LCR within 15 days of the ceremony. [1]
10. Ask the Local Civil Registrar when your marriage record will be forwarded to PSA, then request your PSA marriage certificate once the record is available.
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2012/ra_10354_2012.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: when you do not need a licence
content:
The Family Code exempts some cases, including marriage in danger of death, and a man and woman who have lived together as husband and wife for at least 5 years without any legal impediment to marry. They must sign an affidavit instead. [1]
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: after you apply
content:
- A valid PSA marriage certificate stays valid as long as it is intact and readable (RA 11909). [5]
- A wife may keep her maiden name or use her husband's surname. If she uses his surname on her passport, she must show the PSA marriage certificate. [6]
Source: https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2022/ra_11909_2022.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: Getting married: problems and where to get help
content:
- Licence expired before the wedding: after 120 days the licence lapses, and you must apply again. [1]
- Marriage not yet on PSA records: ask the LCR where the marriage was registered to endorse it to PSA.
- Fees and schedules differ: check your city or municipal Citizen's Charter, which LGUs must publish under RA 11032.
Help: Your city or municipal Civil Registrar. For PSA document issues, use the contacts in the CENOMAR guide.
Source: https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo1987/eo_209_1987.html (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: CENOMAR: who can apply
content:
Who this is for: People who need proof from PSA records that they have never married. It is usually needed to get a marriage licence, and some embassies or employers ask for it too. [5] If you have married before, PSA issues an Advisory on Marriages instead, listing the recorded marriages. [1]
Source: https://legazpi.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/REVISED-CITIZEN-CHARTER-2025-A3.pdf (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: CENOMAR: fees
content:
What it costs: ₱210 at a PSA CRS outlet. [1] With delivery: ₱430 through PSA Serbilis (includes ₱30 documentary stamp tax), or ₱420 through PSAHelpline. [2] [3] A view-only online copy is ₱185. [6]
Source: https://crs-appointment.psahelpline.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: CENOMAR: processing time
content:
How long it takes: 1 working day (8 working hours) at an outlet. [1] Delivery in the Philippines takes about 3 to 9 working days through Serbilis. [2]
Source: https://crs-appointment.psahelpline.ph/ (checked 2026-10-09).

metadata.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, BetterGov.ph; adapted for Kuya J with permission

title: CENOMAR: requirements
content:
- Check that you are allowed to request it. PSA releases a CENOMAR only to the person named, their authorised representative, spouse, parent, direct descendant, guardian or nearest kin (PSA Memorandum Order 2017-050). [2]
- Know the online limits. Online orders through PSAHelpline are only for yourself, your child or your parents. Other requests must go to an outlet. [4]
- Prepare the person's full name, date and place of birth, and parents' names as written on the birth certificate. [2]
- Bring a valid ID. A representative at an outlet also needs the owner's ID and an authorisation letter or SPA. [1]
- Ask the office that wants the CENOMAR how recent your copy must be.
Source: https://crs-itp2.psaserbilis.com.ph/Census/BirthCertificate (checked 2026-10-09).

title: CENOMAR: steps: walk-in
content:

2. Go to the outlet with your ID and slip. [1]
3. Fill in the request form for a Certificate of No Marriage Record. [1]
4. Pay ₱210 per copy. [1]
5. Return on the release date, usually the next working day, to collect it. [1]

content:
